visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video begins with a split-screen composition. The top half shows a controversial advertisement featuring political leaders Hu Jintao and Barack Obama kissing, set against a neutral grey background. The bottom half features a young man with dark hair wearing a black textured blazer over a grey shirt, reacting with a surprised expression in a dimly lit studio with blurred production equipment. (2) The scene cuts to a full-screen view of the young man in the studio, who gestures with his hands while looking directly at the camera. The lighting is focused and professional. (3) A series of graphic overlays and images appear, showcasing Benetton's website and colorful fashion advertisements featuring diverse models of different ages and ethnicities in brightly lit settings. (4) More political kiss advertisements are shown, including Angela Merkel with Nicolas Sarkozy, and Kim Jong-il with Lee Myung-bak, often displayed on large billboards in urban plazas like Milan. (5) A flame graphic effect is overlaid on the narrator as he speaks with intensity. Later, the screen turns to black and white for a brief moment. (6) A promotional segment for a design course follows, showing a middle-aged man in glasses (JL) sitting in a chair, interspersed with artistic shots of a China Airlines airplane, a stylized pink flower blooming, and a grid of corporate logos. (7) The video returns to the narrator, who presents a blurred image of religious leaders kissing with a red heart graphic. He concludes the video by showing a news headline about Benetton withdrawing the ad, with a final shot of himself in front of a blurred Times Square background.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) The audio begins with a male voice speaking at a high speech rate with an excited and sharp pitch, accompanied by high-tempo electronic BGM with a steady 4/4 beat and bright synthesizer textures. (2) As the narrator explains the history of the brand, the BGM continues with consistent energy. Short 'pop' and 'whoosh' sound effects are used to punctuate visual transitions. (3) A distinct 'crackling' fire SFX plays briefly to emphasize the narrator's intensity. (4) A melodic 'ding' bell sound marks a transition into the promotional segment. (5) In the promotional middle section, the BGM shifts to a lower-tempo acoustic arrangement featuring piano and guitar, and a different male voice speaks with a calm, professional, and enunciated tone. (6) The original high-tempo electronic BGM returns along with the primary narrator, who finishes the story with a narrative and slightly comedic tone, maintaining high articulation clarity until the end.
